title: client-migration-assistant-cli-spec-and-integration-requirements
creator: Maya Singh
description: PRD for a client-side Migration Assistant CLI to accelerate and reduce risk for customers moving from legacy unversioned endpoints and model aliases to the Unified Inference API. The tool will detect legacy usage patterns in repos and runtime traffic, generate migration manifests and code/CI patches, and optionally run a non-destructive traffic simulation against a staging endpoint. Goal: reduce manual migration effort and client-support burden while preserving customer uptime during deprecation windows.
scope: Alpha: static code analysis for Python and Node repos to find uses of legacy endpoints (unversioned generate, chatstream, legacy embeddings endpoints)
Alpha: generate a migration manifest (human-editable YAML) that maps legacy endpoints and model aliases to target Unified API calls and model recommendations
Beta: CLI mode to create PRs with suggested code changes for SDK users (redwood-js, redwood-py) and sample patches for direct HTTP clients
Beta: non-destructive live traffic simulation mode for customers with staging keys (proxy that rewrites requests and sends to Unified API in dry-run), with delta telemetry capture
Integrations: CI job template and GitHub Action to run the migrator as a pre-merge check
User flows and UX: guided prompts, migration report, and suggested rollout plan per service/route
out_of_scope: On-prem/private air-gapped deployments that cannot reach our staging endpoints (we will provide a downloadable binary and offline docs but no live simulation)
Automatic schema changes inside customer applications beyond SDK surface (e.g., custom response parsing business logic) — migrator will only provide suggestions and diffs
Full language coverage in Alpha (Java and Go support will be scoped to Beta)
Automated secret rotation for customer API keys during migration; documented manual steps will be provided
acceptance_criteria: Static detector: >=95% recall and >=90% precision on a held-out corpus of 200 internal sample repos that use legacy endpoints
Migration manifest format defined and versioned (manifest v1) and validated by tooling (manifest validator returns exit code 0 for valid manifests)
CLI generates a pull request with suggested code changes for at least 80% of SDK-based usages in test repos (Python/Node) during Beta
Staging simulation: capture and present side-by-side token/cost/latency deltas for simulated requests; simulation run on a representative customer workload within a 6-hour window
CI integration: GitHub Action template runs on sample repo and reports 0 new failing tests introduced by the migrator in 90% of runs
Documentation and quickstart complete: README, example PR, and migration checklist published to docs.redwood.ai before GA
Security review signed off and threat model updated specifically for the simulation proxy and manifest ingestion flows
milestones: Discovery & proto detectors (2025-02-28): finalize endpoint signatures and test corpus
Alpha CLI (2025-03-21): static analysis for Python/Node + manifest generator
Beta (2025-04-18): PR generation, GitHub Action, staging simulation with 3 pilot customers
GA (2025-05-30): public release, docs, and partner enablement
risks: False positives in static detection leading to noisy PRs and developer distrust
Auth/permissions risk if customers accidentally enable live simulation against production keys
Edge-case protocol differences (streaming vs chunked SSE) may not be automatically fixable
Support overhead for pilots if CLI makes unsafe or breaking edits to customer codebases
mitigations: Require explicit --dry-run by default and present human-readable diffs before PR creation
Staging simulation only accepts specially provisioned staging API keys; enforce key prefixes and rate limits
Design the migrator to produce opt-in code comments and TODOs rather than opaque automated replacements for first two releases
Establish a pilot support rota between DevEx and Solutions (two engineer-hours/week during Beta)
dependencies_notes: Requires API compatibility mapping from Model Onboarding and Alias Mapping team (dependency PM-33122)
Telemetry events and sample workloads produced by Routing/Edge team (dependency PM-15234)
Integration with SDK maintainers to generate idiomatic PRs for redwood-js and redwood-py
docs_and_artifacts: GitHub: GH-PRD-91337 (design docs and detector corpus)
Sample manifest schema: docs/migration-manifest-v1.yaml (included in repo)
